takeaway: Headaches, shortness of breath and swelling of the face, upper chest and neck are typical of superior vena cava syndrome from compression by a mediastinal tumour.

lines.text: A sixty-year-old man, a smoker, has a three-day history of worsening headaches.
He is short of breath, and his face, upper chest and neck are swollen.
These symptoms are typical of superior vena cava syndrome.
A mediastinal tumour compresses the superior vena cava.
So the structure being compressed is the superior vena cava.
